room_name: Le palier · The upstairs landing
hook: "ew-mah-nee-TAY": a girl stitches a huge quilt of many hands of every color holding up the world: all of HUMANITY: ew-mah-nee-TAY ≈ HUMANITY
note: Also humaneness, kindness (traiter avec humanité); les humanités = the classics (old school use).

room_name: Le palier · The upstairs landing
hook: "kan-ZEHN": a girl stands perfectly ZEN with about fifteen tin CANs stacked on her head: CAN ZEN: kan-ZEHN ≈ CAN ZEN
note: About fifteen; also two weeks (une quinzaine de jours = a fortnight; la quinzaine commerciale = a two-week sale).

room_name: Le palier · The upstairs landing
hook: "vyeh-YEHS": a very old granny in her rocking chair toots a brass horn to say YES: VIA YES: vyeh-YEHS ≈ VIA YES
note: Old age; can sound blunt about a person, so French often says le grand âge or les seniors.

room_name: Le palier · The upstairs landing
hook: "ah-VUHGL": a cheerful blind man with his white cane and guide dog plays A BUGLE: ah-VUHGL ≈ A BUGLE
note: Un/une aveugle = a blind person; une personne aveugle or non-voyante is the respectful phrasing. Also the adjective blind, and figurative: l'amour est aveugle.

room_name: Le palier · The upstairs landing
hook: "MOHM": a little kid in a giant apron pushes a doll buggy, playing MOM: MOHM ≈ MOM
note: Familiar, a bit slangy (like 'kid'); not for formal speech.

room_name: Le palier · The upstairs landing
hook: "ay-NAY": the oldest brother gives his little brother a piggyback and they both whinny A NEIGH: ay-NAY ≈ A NEIGH
note: L'aîné(e) = the eldest; also as an adjective: mon frère aîné = my older brother.

room_name: Le palier · The upstairs landing
hook: "vyeh-YAHR": a white-bearded old man proudly holds up the YARD-long scarf he knitted: VIA YARD: vyeh-YAHR ≈ VIA YARD
note: Can sound blunt or slightly pejorative; une personne âgée is the polite phrase.

room_name: Le palier · The upstairs landing
hook: "dzhehn-tluh-MAHN": a GENTLEMAN in a bowler hat bows and offers his umbrella to a lady: dzhehn-tluh-MAHN ≈ GENTLEMAN
note: Borrowed from English; often means a well-mannered man, especially an English-speaking one.

room_name: Le palier · The upstairs landing
hook: "SYUHR": a footman bows low with a silver tray: 'Your tea, SIR': SYUHR ≈ SIR
note: Old-fashioned or legal: le sieur Dupont = Mr Dupont in official papers; often ironic today.

room_name: Le salon de coiffure · The hair salon
hook: "MEHSH": a lady's lock of hair pokes out through her MESH highlighting cap: MEHSH ≈ MESH
note: Also a lock of hair (des mèches = highlights), besides a candle wick and a fuse; and a drill bit.

room_name: Le salon de coiffure · The hair salon
hook: "ROO": a red-haired kangaROO sits in the barber chair for a trim: ROO ≈ (kanga)ROO
note: Of hair: red, ginger (un roux = a redhead); a cooking roux too. Teasing about red hair exists, so use it kindly.

room_name: Le salon de coiffure · The hair salon
hook: "SHOHV": a bald man gives the barber a playful SHOVE: there's nothing to cut!: SHOHV ≈ SHOVE
note: Bald; une chauve-souris = a bat (literally a bald mouse). Calling someone chauve can tease.

room_name: Le salon de coiffure · The hair salon
hook: "RAH": a boy with a brand-new buzz cut throws up his arms: RAH!: RAH ≈ RAH!
note: Close-cropped; also level, to the brim (à ras bord); en avoir ras le bol = to be fed up.

room_name: Le salon de coiffure · The hair salon
hook: "bahr-BEW": a tiny bluebird pops out of a man's huge BEARD: BOO!: bahr-BEW ≈ BEARD-BOO
note: Bearded; un barbu = a bearded man, sometimes slang for a religious hard-liner, so be careful.

room_name: Le salon de coiffure · The hair salon
hook: "boo-KLAY": a curly-haired girl sculpts a head of BLUE CLAY with curls: boo-KLAY ≈ BLUE CLAY
note: Curly; also buckled (bouclé = fastened); une boucle = a curl, a buckle or a loop.

room_name: Le salon de coiffure · The hair salon
hook: "koh-MEEK": a boy under the big hood dryer laughs at a COMIC book: koh-MEEK ≈ COMIC
note: Funny, comical; un comique = a comedian; a comic book is une BD.

room_name: Le salon de coiffure · The hair salon
hook: "TAN": a beautician holds a palette of powder shades to a man's cheek to match his complexion: TAN, TAN, TAN: TAN ≈ (shade) TAN
note: Complexion; also the shade of a dyed fabric; also the past participle of teindre (to dye).

room_name: La salle des cartes · The map room
hook: "kah-nah-DYAN": DIANE pours a CAN of maple syrup over her pancakes: CAN-A-DIANE: kah-nah-DYAN ≈ CAN-A-DIANE
note: Canadian; capitalized as a noun (un Canadien). Une canadienne can also mean a fleece-lined jacket.

room_name: La salle des cartes · The map room
hook: "lohn-doh-NYAN": a boy gives a huge YAWN next to a little model of LONDON's Big Ben: lohn-doh-NYAN ≈ LONDON-YAWN
note: Of or from London; un Londonien = a Londoner.

room_name: La salle des cartes · The map room
hook: "mah-gray-BAN": MA in a GRAY headBAND points to North Africa on the wall map: mah-gray-BAN ≈ MA GRAY BAN(d)
note: From the Maghreb (Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia); a neutral origin word, capitalized as a noun (un Maghrébin).

room_name: La salle des cartes · The map room
hook: "oh-ree-zhee-NEHR": a toy hot-AIR balloon rises from its ORIGIN pin on the big map: ORIGIN-AIR: oh-ree-zhee-NEHR ≈ ORIGIN-AIR
note: Used with de: originaire de Lyon = from Lyon, native of Lyon; it means coming from, not original (= original).

room_name: La salle des cartes · The map room
hook: "ee-SEW": grandpa SEWs a family-tree quilt where every branch comes from the trunk: HE SEWS: ee-SEW ≈ HE SEW(s)
note: Used with de: issu de = coming from, born of (issu d'une famille modeste); une issue = an exit or outcome.

room_name: La salle des cartes · The map room
hook: "zhee-TAHN": a smiling traveler spreads TONS of postcards over southern France and Spain: GEE, TONS!: zhee-TAHN ≈ GEE, TON(s)!
note: A Romani person, especially in Spain and southern France (capitalized: un Gitan, une Gitane). It can be pejorative depending on who says it and how; Rom (or Romani) is the neutral term.

room_name: La salle des trésors · The treasure room
hook: "doh-RAY": a DOE stands in a golden RAY of sunlight and shines like gold: DOE-RAY: doh-RAY ≈ DOE RAY
note: Golden or gilded; also browned in cooking (bien doré = nicely golden); la jeunesse dorée = gilded rich youth.

room_name: La salle des trésors · The treasure room
hook: "fah-bew-LEUH": a little dragon flies right out of a giant FABLE book: FABUL-ous: fah-bew-LEUH ≈ FABUL(ous)
note: Also fabled, legendary (un animal fabuleux = a creature from fables).

room_name: La salle des trésors · The treasure room
hook: "an-pray-syoh-NAHN": AN ANT lifts a huge golden trophy over its head: how IMPRESSIVE: an-pray-syoh-NAHN ≈ IMPRESS-ive... AN ANT
note: Impressive; can also mean frightening or overwhelming (une foule impressionnante).

room_name: La salle des trésors · The treasure room
hook: "spehk-tah-kew-LEHR": a giant pair of sparkling SPECTACLES floats in the AIR: SPECTACLE-AIR: spehk-tah-kew-LEHR ≈ SPECTACLE-AIR
note: Spectacular; un spectacle = a show, a performance.

room_name: La salle des trésors · The treasure room
hook: "vee-ZEEBL": a bright pink chameleon on a green plant is VISIBLE to everyone: vee-ZEEBL ≈ VISIBLE
note: Also obvious; of a person: available, willing to see visitors (Monsieur n'est pas visible).

room_name: La salle des trésors · The treasure room
hook: "sahn-BLAHBL": two wobbly jelly BLOBs on a plate look almost the SAME: SAME-BLOB-le: sahn-BLAHBL ≈ SAME BLOB-le
note: Similar, alike; mes semblables = my fellow human beings.

room_name: La salle des trésors · The treasure room
hook: "ay-toh-NAHN": a girl rings A TONE on the glass harp and ANN gasps: A TONE, ANN!: ay-toh-NAHN ≈ A TONE, ANN!
note: Surprising, amazing; often just surprising: ce n'est pas étonnant = no wonder.

room_name: La salle d'attente · The waiting room
hook: "an-pah-SYAHN": a man taps his foot and checks his watch for the tenth time: so IMPATIENT: an-pah-SYAHN ≈ IMPATIENT
note: Also eager: impatient de te voir = looking forward to seeing you.

room_name: La salle d'attente · The waiting room
hook: "pray-SAY": a lady in a hurry gulps a glass of fresh-PRESSED juice on the way: PRESS-AY: pray-SAY ≈ PRESS-AY
note: In a hurry; also pressed or squeezed: un citron pressé = fresh lemon juice.

room_name: La salle d'attente · The waiting room
hook: "pah-reh-SEUH": a sloth hangs from the coat rack and RESTS: PAH, REST, UH: pah-reh-SEUH ≈ PAH, REST-UH
note: Lazy; un paresseux is also the sloth itself.

room_name: La salle d'attente · The waiting room
hook: "ay-zee-TAHN": a little boy reaches one HESITANT finger toward a huge shaggy sheepdog: ay-zee-TAHN ≈ HESITANT
note: Also shaky, unsteady (une voix hésitante = a faltering voice).

room_name: La salle d'attente · The waiting room
hook: "day-zehs-pay-RAY": a man with wild hair drops to his knees and begs for a haircut: DESPERATE: day-zehs-pay-RAY ≈ DESPERATE
note: Desperate, but also hopeless (un cas désespéré = a hopeless case).

room_name: La salle d'attente · The waiting room
hook: "mah-lah-DRWAH": a clumsy boy trips on his laces and knocks over the tall magazine stack: MALADROIT: mah-lah-DRWAH ≈ MAL-A-DROIT
note: Clumsy; also tactless (une remarque maladroite = a clumsy remark).

room_name: La salle d'attente · The waiting room
hook: "ah-VEED": a wide-eyed girl devours magazine after magazine: an AVID reader: ah-VEED ≈ AVID
note: Eager, avid, but often greedy: avide d'argent = greedy for money.

room_name: La salle d'attente · The waiting room
hook: "ahn-bee-SYEUH": a little girl stands on the shelf and stretches up to reach the very top: so AMBITIOUS: ahn-bee-SYEUH ≈ AMBITIOUS
note: Ambitious; can also suggest pretentious (un projet trop ambitieux = overambitious).

room_name: La salle à manger · The dining room
hook: "ahd-mee-RAHBL": a boy hands his own big slice of pie to his little sister: how ADMIRABLE: ahd-mee-RAHBL ≈ ADMIRABLE
note: Admirable, wonderful; can be ironic (d'une admirable mauvaise foi).

room_name: La salle à manger · The dining room
hook: "eh-MAHBL": a likeable girl hands A MARBLE to every guest: A-MARBLE: eh-MAHBL ≈ A MARBLE
note: Kind, likeable; vous êtes bien aimable = that's very kind of you (also said ironically).

room_name: La salle à manger · The dining room
hook: "shah-leuh-REUH": a grandma wraps a warm SHAWL round a shivering guest: SHAWL-ER-UH: shah-leuh-REUH ≈ SHAWL-ER-UH
note: Warm and welcoming (of people, places, applause); not used for temperature: hot = chaud.

room_name: La salle à manger · The dining room
hook: "oh-NEHT": an HONEST boy hands back a wallet someone dropped: oh-NEHT ≈ HONEST
note: Honest, but also decent, acceptable (un salaire honnête = a fair salary); un honnête homme = a cultivated gentleman (old).

room_name: La salle à manger · The dining room
hook: "san-SEHR": a boy puts his hand on his heart to say a SINCERE sorry: san-SEHR ≈ SINCERE
note: Sincere; in letters: mes sincères condoléances = my sincere condolences.

room_name: La salle à manger · The dining room
hook: "ah-mee-KAHL": a friendly boy waves and CALLS his AMI to the seat beside him: AMI-CALL: ah-mee-KAHL ≈ AMI CALL
note: Friendly; un match amical = a friendly (game).

room_name: La salle à manger · The dining room
hook: "oh-tahn-TEEK": grandpa shows off his real old gramophone: OH, ANTIQUE!: oh-tahn-TEEK ≈ OH, (an)TIQUE!
note: Authentic, genuine; also of a person: real, not fake.

room_name: La salle à manger · The dining room
hook: "reh-zoh-NAHBL": grandpa pours two exactly equal glasses of lemonade: fair and REASON-ABLE: reh-zoh-NAHBL ≈ REASON-ABLE
note: Reasonable, sensible; also fair (un prix raisonnable); of a child: sensible, well-behaved (sois raisonnable!).

room_name: Le hall d'entrée · The entrance hall
change: door added: staircase up to palier (Le palier · The landing)
